final.summary: The ETP stopped for maintenance in the afternoon, but the equalization tank rose while outfall flow stayed at zero and pH stayed near neutral, showing the water was held. Power matched the expected load over the full treatment interval and the power feed was not a replay, with a meter photo confirming standby power during the stop. After restart the outfall stayed near neutral, consistent with treated effluent.

explanations.label: ETP stopped for maintenance with wastewater held in equalization tank
Aeration cut / low power with normal inflow

key_evidence.why: Power at standby level through the stop confirms the ETP was stopped.
Tank level rose while ETP was at standby, showing inflow was stored.
Zero outfall flow during the stop shows nothing passed the outfall meter then.
Tank balance within tolerance shows arriving water was stored, not bypassed.
Outfall pH stayed near neutral during the stop, showing no raw wastewater at the outfall.
Power matched the expected band for inflow over the full treatment interval.
Power feed did not repeat another day, ruling out a replayed feed.
Meter photo reading matches the feed, confirming standby power was real.
Neutral pH after restart shows treated effluent, not raw discharge.

final.scope_line: Based on intake, ETP inflow, power, tank level, outfall flow, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: No lab BOD result was available in the case period, so organic pollutant removal is inferred from power, flow and pH, not directly measured.
Outfall flow and ETP inflow were flat at zero through the stop; a stuck meter reading zero would look the same, but the tank rise, intake volume and pH together show the water was held.
Conductivity after restart was not checked within the remaining checks, so salt tracking there is not assessed.
Factory logbook and maintenance record are claims checked against signals, not facts.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels).
